(By pleader Usha K)
 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.40,00,000/ for the death of Shivaraju S/o Nanjegowda in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 18.06.2020 at about 5.30 p.m., when the deceased Suresh was walking on the left side of the road and when he reached near Elerampura road, S.Gollahalli Village, at that time, one Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA13T6471 was driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed against the deceased.
Due to the impact, Shivaraju was died on the spot.
The Petitioners have spent about Rs.4,00,000/ towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as Coolie cum Agriculturist and Milk Vendor and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Shivaraju, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA13T6471.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its detailed Objection Statement interalia denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also injuries sustained by the deceased in the said accident.

Further it contended that, at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective Smt. Nilamma vs Sri. B.R.Hemesh on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180537496/
2 driving license.
Therefore it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

On these grounds,
Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Shivaraju S/o Nanjegowda?
2. Whether Petitioners prove his age and earnings as stated in the petition?

3. Whether the Petitioners prove that Shivaraju sustained injuries due to rash and negligent act of driving of Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA13T6471 on dated 18.06.2020 at about 5.30 P.M and succumbed to the injuries?
4.
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
5. What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 13 and closed her side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.2 got examined one witness as RW.1 and closed its side evidence.

6. Having heard both the sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : In the Affirmative Issue No.4 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.5 : As per the Final Order for the following :

REASONS 7. Issue No.3: It is the case of the Petitioners that the Shivaraju was died in the accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA13T 6471.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tractor.

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and reiterated the averments made in the petition.

Smt. Nilamma vs Sri. B.R.Hemesh on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180537496/
3 10.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW1 has relied on Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.

Ex.P1 and 2 are the True copies of FIR and Complaint which shows that the Kolala Police have registered the case against the driver of Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA13T6471 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the Spot mahazar and Ex.P4 is the Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of PM report which shows the cause of death is due to shock and Haemorrage.

Ex.P7 is the true copy of the ChargeSheet which shows that the Kolala Police has submitted Charge sheet against the driver of the offending Tractor for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A).

The Column No.17 of the Charge Sheet reads as under:
" 18.06.2020   5.30      ,   .    
         
  12    136471          
        
        
      01             
    01        01             , ,  , ,    
       
        ."
11.
PW1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2.

But nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
12.
To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Respondent No.2 has examined the driver of the offending tractor by name Manjunath.
Charge sheet is the material document which was submitted by the I.O after thorough investigation.

Hence, the Petitioners have proved that the said accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending tractor and in the said accident, the husband of PW.1 was succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 is "in the Affirmative ".
13. Issue No.1, 2 and 4: All these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
14.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased, Petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children of the deceased and Respondent No.5 is the mother of the deceased Shivaraju.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced Aadhar cards of deceased and Petitioners at Ex.P.8 to P.13.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.

As the Petitioners are Smt. Nilamma vs Sri. B.R.Hemesh on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180537496/
4 the L.Rs of deceased Shivaraju, they entitled for the compensation.
15. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 41 years and deceased was working as Coolie, Agriculturist cum Milk Vendor and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
But PW.1 has not produced any document for income proof of the deceased.
Therefore, in the absence of actual income proof, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since, the accident has occurred in the year 2020, the income of the deceased is notionally taken at Rs.14,500/ p.m., for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
16. Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Shivaraju as 41 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.8 i.e., the Aadhar Card of the deceased Shivaraju which shows his date of birth as 01.01.1975.
The alleged accident was occurred on 18.06.2020.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Shivaraju was 46 years.
Hence, the age of the deceased Shivaraju to be taken at 46 years for the purpose of assessment.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
18.
The deceased has left behind his wife, daughters, son and mother.

The Petitioner No.1 is the wife,
Petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children and Petitioner No.5 is the mother and they are considered as dependents on the deceased

. At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children and Petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased Shivaraju are entitled for a sum of Rupees 40,000/ towards loss of consortium and Rupees 15,000/ towards loss of estate and Rupees 15,000/ towards funeral expenses.
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
19.

Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and support in her young age and Petitioner No.2 to 4 are the minor children of deceased and they have lost father's love and care in their young age and the Petitioner No.5 is the mother of deceased Shivaraju, who lost son's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:

Smt. Nilamma vs Sri. B.R.Hemesh on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180537496/
5 20.
The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
21.

It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was at Rs.14,500/ pm.
22.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s. Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn.
Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment  Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects " 
Held :  yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
 "Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of  assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40  Upholding objections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation - Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held: Yes: there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork:
executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil)
No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 25% when the age is between 40 to 50 years".

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 46 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 25% of the income has to be added.
So, 25% of Rs. 14,500/ comes to Rs.3,625/.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.18,125/ p.m.
Smt. Nilamma vs Sri. B.R.Hemesh on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180537496/
6 (Rs.14,500/ + Rs.3,625/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 13.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family members is 4 to 6. 1/4th of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

23. After deducting 1/4th towards his personal expenses in Rs.18,125/ it comes to Rs.13,594/
(Rs.18,125/  4,531/) and multiplier applied is 13 which comes to Rs.21,20,664/ (13,594 x 12 x 13).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,20,664/ towards loss of dependency.

24. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 15,000/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/ of dead body 6.
Loss of Dependency Rs.21,20,664/ Total Rs.22,45,664/
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.22,45,664/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

25. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA13T6471.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Further, the Respondent No.2 admitted the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending lorry.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 and 2 are "in the Affirmative" and Issue No.4 "Partly in the Affirmative".
26. Issue No.5:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 5 are entitled for compensation of Rs.22,45,664/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

7

The Petitioner No.1 to 5 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.22,45,664/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 5 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 40% to the Petitioner No.1.
2) 15% each to the Petitioner No.2 to 5.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 and 2 by way of Epayment and after their proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 and 2 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.3 and 4 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank till they attains age of majority.

Further,
the natural guardian/mother of the minor Petitioner No.3 and 4 is permitted to withdraw the interest on the said Fixed deposit periodically to the best interest of the minor Petitioners.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.5 is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.5 by way of E payment and after her proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
